AD.summary: Andorra is a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement (in force 10 March 2007), so a coffin from another party state travels on the laissez-passer for a corpse issued in the country of death. Andorra has no jet airport: the coffin lands in Spain (usually Barcelona) or France and continues by road, and the Spanish or French entry formalities apply at that airport.

at_a_glance.embalming: Per departure country; Spain wants conservation certificate
at_a_glance.permit: Sanidad Exterior entry if landing in Spain
at_a_glance.arrival: Land in Spain or France, then road

steps.what: Appoint funeral directors in the country of death and in Andorra; choose the arrival airport (Barcelona or Toulouse).
Obtain the death certificate, embalming or conservation and the sealed zinc-lined coffin.
Obtain the laissez-passer for a corpse (Strasbourg states) or the Spanish consulate's Documento Unico (other countries).
Spanish funeral company requests the Sanidad Exterior entry authorisation through SISAEX.
Customs release at the airport, then road transfer to Andorra by the Andorran funeral director.

key_points: Strasbourg Agreement party since 10 March 2007
No jet airport: Spanish or French entry rules apply at the airport
Andorran laissez-passer issuer: Servei de Medicina Forense

Sealed zinc-lined coffin (Strasbourg standard)
Road transfer to a Spanish or French airport
Non-Strasbourg destinations: their consulate's approval
AD.private_jet_note: No jet airport in Andorra: land in Spain or France, clear their health formalities, then transfer by road.

AE.summary: Bringing a casket into the UAE goes through the UAE embassy or consulate in the country of death, which attests the death certificate and its Arabic translation; detailed import rules for non-nationals are not published, so confirm with the consulate. Leaving the UAE requires police no-objection letters, an attested death certificate, embalming and the home embassy's no-objection letter.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Attested by UAE embassy, Arabic translation

steps.what: Contact the UAE embassy or consulate in the country of death and appoint funeral directors at both ends.
Obtain the local death certificate, cause-of-death report and embalming certificate.
Have the death certificate legalised and translated into Arabic, then attested by the UAE embassy.
Seal the casket, book the flight and send copies to the receiving UAE funeral service.
Customs and health clearance at the airport, collection by the funeral service, burial.

key_points: Official UAE guidance covers UAE nationals dying abroad; for others confirm with the consulate
Procedures can vary by emirate, religion and residency status
Exit needs MOFA-stamped death certificate and embassy no-objection letter

Police no-objection letters for mortuary, embalming and airport
Embassy no-objection letter and cancelled passport
Embalming certificate; 7 copies of each document

AL.summary: A casket entering Albania needs a body transport permit (laissez-passer) issued by the Albanian embassy or consulate in the country of death, on presentation of the apostilled death certificate and the deceased's passport or ID. Repatriation is handled by funeral directors; the casket arrives sealed and is released to an Albanian funeral home.

Apostille the death certificate in the country of death.
Present apostilled certificate and passport at the Albanian consulate; laissez-passer issued.
Casket prepared, sealed and booked on the flight.
Airport clearance and handover to the Albanian funeral home.

key_points: Apostille comes before the consular permit
Not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses
No cremation in Albania

Special transport casket and passport required
No cremation available in Albania
Ask for the international death certificate
AL.private_jet_note: Keep the consular laissez-passer and apostilled death certificate with the casket.

AO.summary: Before departure, the Angolan consulate in the country of death reviews a transfer (trasladação) file: legalised death certificate, transport permit from the local authority and a health certificate. The casket then travels with these originals to Luanda.

at_a_glance.arrival: Customs and health clearance in Luanda

steps.what: Register the death locally and obtain the full death certificate and medical health certificate.
Obtain the local transport permit (e.g. PSP alvara in Portugal) and have all documents legalised and translated into Portuguese.
File the trasladacao request at the Angolan consulate with originals and copies.
Consulate processes the file (Lisbon: 8 working days, no fee).
Casket sealed by the funeral director and flown with the original documents.
Customs and health clearance in Luanda; local funeral agent collects the casket.

key_points: Every document must be legalised; missing papers can lead to refusal
Allow about 8 working days at the consulate
Casket specifications are not published: confirm with the consulate
Not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement on the transfer of corpses, so a laissez-passer alone does not suffice.

Death registration at the Civil Registration Office is mandatory

Morgue storage conditions vary by region

AR.summary: Argentine consulates do not issue a repatriation permit: the funeral home in the country of death prepares apostilled documents (death certificate, non-contagious disease certificate, embalming and sealed-coffin certificate) that travel with the coffin, and files the entry request with Argentine authorities.

at_a_glance.coffin: Sealed, waterproof coffin certified by funeral home
at_a_glance.consular: Apostille only; consulate issues no permit
at_a_glance.permit: Argentine funeral home files entry request
at_a_glance.arrival: Argentine funeral home clears customs and health

Obtain the death certificate and a health authority certificate of no contagious disease
Embalming and placement in a sealed waterproof coffin; funeral home certificate issued

Receiving funeral home clears customs and health and arranges burial or cremation

Every foreign document needs a Hague apostille
Embalming report required by the New York consulate
Confirm current health filing rules with the receiving funeral home

Judicial release needed when a court is involved
Apostille as required by destination country

AS.summary: A US territory: remains arriving from abroad fall under US federal (CDC) import rules, which apply to American Samoa. Non-cremated remains must be in a leak-proof container and, unless embalmed, travel with a death certificate stating the cause of death; local health approval should be confirmed.

at_a_glance.permit: CDC permit only for infectious cases
at_a_glance.arrival: Directly to a licensed funeral home

steps.what: Appoint a receiving funeral home in Tutuila and ask it about any local clearance.
Obtain the death certificate (with cause) and, for US citizens abroad, the consular mortuary documents.
Place the remains in a leak-proof container; embalm if required by the airline.
Fly into Pago Pago with the original documents.
Customs clearance; remains go directly to the licensed funeral home.

key_points: US federal CDC import rules apply to the territory (42 CFR 71.1)
Embalmed remains need no death certificate under CDC rules
Local customs and health clearance not published: confirm locally
export_points: Death certificate via the Office of Vital Statistics
Local export clearance not published; confirm locally
Check the destination country's requirements

AT.summary: A coffin entering Austria must carry a corpse laissez-passer (Leichenpass) from the competent authority of the place of death, or one issued by an Austrian embassy or consulate. Austrian customs check the Leichenpass and the coffin on arrival, including on flights from other EU countries.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Required from the country of death
at_a_glance.laissez_passer: Leichenpass required from place of death

steps.what: Appoint local and Austrian funeral companies; obtain death certificate
Preparation and sealing in zinc-lined coffin
Leichenpass from the local authority or Austrian mission
Flight to Austria; customs check Leichenpass and coffin
Austrian funeral company handles burial or cremation under state law

key_points: Leichenpass checked even on intra-EU transfers
Rules and fees vary by federal state

Death registered and Totenbeschau completed first
Only licensed funeral companies may transport
Destination country may require further documents

AU.summary: Human remains may be brought into Australia for burial or cremation without an import declaration, provided official documentation such as a copy of the death certificate travels with them; without it, official permission is needed. An Australian funeral director or customs broker should be engaged to manage human biosecurity clearance on arrival.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Copy stating cause must accompany remains
at_a_glance.embalming: Required by origin country and airline

steps.what: Appoint a funeral director in the country of death and one in Australia.
Obtain the death certificate stating the cause of death and the local export permit.
Embalming and sealing in a hermetically sealed coffin; airline booking.
Australian funeral director or customs broker notifies the department (48 hours preferred) and prepares biosecurity clearance.
Biosecurity and border clearance; funeral director collects the coffin.
Burial or cremation under state or territory rules.

key_points: Missing death certificate means biosecurity officer permission is needed first.
No import declaration is needed for remains for burial or cremation.
Ashes need no import permit; avoid wooden urns.

export_points: Death certificate and medical certificate of cause of death
Embalming certificate (or freezing/dry ice if destination accepts)
State health transit or repatriation letter, about 48 hours notice
Coroner's release order for coroner's cases
AU.private_jet_note: Arrange biosecurity clearance in advance and have a funeral director meet the aircraft.

AW.summary: The Landsbesluit lijkenvervoer (AB 1993 GT 36, implementing art. 40 of the Begrafenisverordening) allows a body to be brought into Aruba if it is embalmed or otherwise preserved, sealed in a hermetic impermeable coffin with absorbent material inside a sound outer case, labelled, and accompanied by a medical/death statement, an embalming statement and a transport statement from the authority of the place of death. Burial must take place as soon as possible with written leave from the civil registrar.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Death statement or certificate extract required
at_a_glance.consular: No consular step set by law
at_a_glance.permit: Civil registrar burial leave on arrival

steps.what: Funeral home at origin obtains death certificate/medical statement and embalms the body.
Origin authority issues transport permit stating route; documents apostilled if needed.
Body sealed in hermetic coffin inside outer case, labelled with identity and destination.

key_points: Hermetic sealing and preservation are legal requirements, so a pouch alone is not acceptable

Burial must take place as soon as possible after arrival

AZ.summary: No official Azerbaijani rules for bringing a casket in were found; confirm with the Azerbaijani consulate in the country of death. For deaths in Azerbaijan, a compulsory autopsy, the AZS-106 medical death certificate, the civil death certificate and a coroner's release are needed before the body can leave.

AZS-106 then civil death certificate

BA.summary: A casket entering Bosnia and Herzegovina needs a BiH laissez-passer (certificate for the transfer of human remains) issued by the BiH embassy or consulate in the country of death, plus a transport request for the entity health ministry of the burial place (Federation of BiH, Republika Srpska or Brcko District). The body must travel in a hermetically sealed, metal-lined (zinc) casket.

at_a_glance.coffin: Sealed metal-lined casket in air tray

Permission to remove the body and passport

No crematorium in BiH

BD.summary: A casket can enter Bangladesh with a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Bangladesh embassy or consulate in the country of death. The NOC is issued on the death certificate, the passport and, after an accident, a police or autopsy report. The family must name the person who will receive the body at the airport.

BE.summary: Belgium applies the Strasbourg Agreement, so a coffin from another party state travels on the departure country's laissez-passer in a sealed zinc-lined coffin. at_a_glance.coffin: Sealed coffin; confirm with consulate and airline

BH.summary: For Bahraini nationals, Bahrain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a 'Transferring Bahraini deceased bodies' service through its embassies: a family request letter, passport copy and a death certificate legalised by the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of death, processed in 3 working days. CH.summary: Switzerland is a party to the Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin agreement, so a coffin from another party state travels on the departure country's laissez-passer in a sealed zinc-lined coffin. at_a_glance.coffin: Soldered zinc inner coffin or lining

steps.what: Appoint funeral directors; obtain death certificate
Embalming if required; coffin sealed; laissez-passer issued
Flight to Switzerland; customs clearance at arrival airport
Swiss funeral director handles cantonal burial or cremation

key_points: Swiss customs apply even from the EU
Leichenpass issuer moved to civil registry offices in 2025

Sealed zinc-lined coffin
Cantonal procedures differ

CI.summary: Before a casket can be flown to Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivorian consulate in the country of death issues a body transfer authorisation (autorisation de transfert de corps). The funeral home files it with the death record, medical, non-contagion, non-epidemic and embalming certificates, the coffining record, the local transport authorisation and mortuary laissez-passer, and proof of identity (Ivorian embassy in Paris: EUR 10 fee).

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Full copy of the death record

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home; it gathers the death record and medical certificates.
Embalming, coffining and closing of the coffin, with the coffining record.

In France: the funeral company obtains the préfet's transport authorisation (and an ARS certificate of non-epidemic if the prefecture asks for it) and seals the coffin in a hermetic metal-lined casket.

Flight to Abidjan with all originals.
Customs and health clearance, then an Ivorian funeral home or the family collects the casket.

Cremation is not permitted in Côte d'Ivoire

CK.summary: Under the Public Health Act 2004, remains brought into the Cook Islands for burial or cremation must be kept embalmed and in a sealed, impervious container, and must be buried or cremated within 48 hours of arrival unless the Secretary of Health grants a written exemption.

at_a_glance.consular: No consular permit in the law

steps.what: Contact Te Marae Ora (Ministry of Health) and the family in the Cook Islands to set the funeral date.
Embalm, seal the casket and gather the death certificate and embalming and sealing certificates.
If burial cannot happen within 48 hours of arrival, apply to the Secretary of Health for a written exemption.
Fly to Rarotonga with the original documents.
Burial or cremation, unless an exemption has been granted.

key_points: Embalming and a sealed casket are legal requirements
Burial within 48 hours of arrival unless exempted
Outgoing remains must leave within 48 hours
export_points: Embalm and seal within 24 hours of receipt
Remains must leave the Cook Islands within 48 hours
Exemptions only by written decision of the Secretary of Health
CK.private_jet_note: Burial within 48 hours of arrival is a legal requirement; have the funeral ready before take-off.

CL.summary: Under Chile's General Cemeteries Regulation (Decree 357 of 1970), a body may enter Chile only with documents from the health authority of the place of origin, endorsed by the Chilean consul, showing the transport poses no public health risk, and with authorisation of the competent Regional Ministerial Health Secretary (SEREMI de Salud).

at_a_glance.arrival: Funeral home collects; SEREMI authorises transfer

steps.what: Contact the Chilean consulate and appoint funeral homes at both ends
Obtain death certificate and health authority document stating no public health risk
Embalming and sealing in an impermeable hermetic coffin
Chilean consul endorses (or apostille) the documents; SEREMI de Salud authorisation requested
Chilean funeral home collects the coffin and obtains the burial pass

key_points: Health documents must be endorsed by the Chilean consul
Coffin must travel in a separate compartment
Health authority seal must stay intact to destination
Ashes need no health authorisation if in a closed urn

Coffin travels in a separate compartment of the aircraft
Judicial release needed after violent or unexplained death
Usually one to two weeks

CM.summary: A Certificate of Repatriation (mortuary laissez-passer) must be obtained from the Cameroonian embassy or high commission in the country of death, applied for and paid on the evisacam.cm portal. The UK mission also requires a regional authorisation signed by the Prefect for entry into Douala or Yaounde.

Embalming and free-from-infection certificate; local removal permit.
Upload documents and pay the fee on evisacam.cm (Laissez-Passer section); the Berlin embassy asks for this at least 7 days before departure.
Mission examines the file and issues the Certificate of Repatriation / mortuary laissez-passer (Berlin: indicative 7 days).
Coffin sealed and flown with the original documents.
Clearance at Douala or Yaounde; family or funeral home collects.

Applications and fees go through evisacam.cm
UK mission requires a Prefect-signed regional authorisation

Cause-of-death certificate usually within a week
Agree costs in writing beforehand
Autopsy reports can be slow
CM.private_jet_note: Consular laissez-passer via evisacam.cm and Prefect's authorisation needed before take-off.

CN.summary: Cross-border transport of a body is allowed only for funeral or medical purposes and must be handled by the China Funeral Association's international body transport service centre or a local funeral home. Entry needs approval from the civil affairs and foreign affairs authorities and an entry permit from border quarantine (customs).

at_a_glance.permit: Quarantine entry permit and civil affairs approval

Embalming, encoffining, death certificate legalisation abroad (confirm requirements with the carrier)
Approval by Chinese civil affairs or foreign affairs authorities obtained
Declaration to border quarantine (customs) for the entry permit
Quarantine check and customs release; designated carrier takes the casket

CO.summary: Colombia's Ministry of Health Resolution 717 of 21 April 2026 now regulates international transfers: an embalmed body in a hermetically sealed inner coffin, IATA/ISPM-15 packaging, and a documentary check by the departmental, district or municipal health authority at the airport of arrival, which signs the entry authorisation form. at_a_glance.coffin: Hermetic inner coffin, ISPM-15 outer packaging
at_a_glance.laissez_passer: Not used; Colombia not Strasbourg party

at_a_glance.permit: Health authority signs form at airport
at_a_glance.arrival: Document check, then funeral home collects

Death certificate (apostilled, translated), embalming, hermetic sealing and ISPM-15 outer packaging

Health authority checks documents and signs the Annex 7 form; funeral home collects the coffin

key_points: Resolution 717 of 2026 sets air transport rules
Embalming is mandatory for every air transfer

Embalming mandatory for any air transport

CR.summary: Costa Rican health law requires any body moved internationally to be embalmed and placed in an impermeable, hermetically closed coffin, with an official death certificate, a preparation (embalming) declaration, a sworn statement that the coffin holds only the deceased, and a transit permit. The receiving funeral home clears the coffin and must organise burial quickly, as burial normally takes place within 24-36 hours unless the Ministry of Health extends the deadline.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Official certificate with cause of death
at_a_glance.laissez_passer: Transit permit from place of death
at_a_glance.consular: Apostille and official translation for registration

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home at each end and contact the Costa Rican consulate.
Obtain the death certificate with cause of death, embalming certificate and transit permit at origin.
Sign a sworn statement that the coffin holds only the deceased; seal the embalmed body in a hermetic coffin with a name plate.
Receiving funeral home asks the Ministry of Health area office for a burial-deadline extension.
Fly with document copies attached to the coffin and originals in hand.
Customs and health clearance; funeral home collects for burial or cremation.

key_points: Embalming and a hermetically closed coffin are legal requirements
Burial normally within 24-36 hours unless the Ministry of Health extends it
Metal coffins cannot be buried in the ground; check with the cemetery

Hermetically closed impermeable coffin
Autopsy usual unless natural death over age 75

CU.summary: To bring a body into Cuba, the death must first be transcribed at the Cuban consulate, and the embalming certificate, burial licence and health ministry authorisation for the transfer (with official Spanish translations) must be authenticated by the foreign ministry of the country of death and then legalised by the Cuban consulate, which also issues a declaration on the preparation of the body. The family must also contact the Funeraria de Calzada y K in Havana.

at_a_glance.consular: Authentication then Cuban legalisation; fees vary
at_a_glance.arrival: Funeraria de Calzada y K, Havana

steps.what: Contact the Cuban consulate for the place of death and a funeral home there.
Embalming; obtain the burial licence and health ministry transfer authorisation.
Official Spanish translations; authentication by the foreign ministry of the country of death.
Cuban consulate transcribes the death, legalises documents and issues its declaration.

CV.summary: Cabo Verde's Decreto-Lei 15/2015 governs bodies arriving from abroad: the transfer document (alvará) must be endorsed by the Conservador dos Registos Centrais (or the registrar of the island of entry), the death record is transcribed in Cabo Verde, and burial or cremation must take place within 72 hours of entry.

steps.what: Obtain the death certificate and the transfer permit in the country of death; contact a funeral home in Cabo Verde.
Embalming and sealing of the coffin (zinc if a vault burial is planned).
Send the death record and transfer permit for endorsement by the Conservatória dos Registos Centrais; reserve the cemetery.
Pack the coffin in an opaque case marked 'handle with care' and book the flight.
Customs and health clearance; burial within 72 hours of entry.

key_points: Decreto-Lei 15/2015 regulates transfers from abroad
Registrar must endorse the transfer permit

Certificates only in Portuguese

CW.summary: The Landsbesluit implementing art. 40 of the Begrafenisverordening (P.B. 1975 no. 46, consolidated text P.B. 2025 no. 145) allows a body to be brought into Curaçao if it is embalmed or otherwise preserved, sealed in a hermetic coffin of impermeable material with absorbent material inside a sound outer coffin, labelled, and accompanied by a medical/death statement, an embalming statement and a transport statement from the authority of the place of death. Burial must take place as soon as possible with written leave from the civil registrar.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Death statement or certificate extract required
at_a_glance.consular: No consular step set by law
at_a_glance.permit: Civil registrar burial leave on arrival

steps.what: Funeral home at origin obtains the death certificate/medical statement and embalms or preserves the body.
Origin authority issues a statement on how and by which route the body will travel.
Body sealed in a hermetic coffin inside an outer coffin, labelled with identity and destination.
The three statements are presented on arrival; local funeral home collects.
Civil registrar issues free written burial leave; burial as soon as possible.

key_points: Hermetic sealing and preservation are legal requirements, so a pouch alone is not acceptable
Curaçao has its own legislation within the Kingdom of the Netherlands (text consolidated in 2025)
Burial must take place as soon as possible after arrival, with free written leave from the civil registrar

CY.summary: Cyprus is a party to the Strasbourg Agreement; its competent authority for the laissez-passer for a corpse is the Director of the Department of Medical Services, Ministry of Health. A coffin from another party state travels on the departure country's laissez-passer in a hermetically sealed coffin meeting the Agreement's standard; rules for coffins from non-party countries are not published online.

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Required; issued in Greek, Turkish, English

steps.what: Appoint funeral directors; obtain death certificate

CZ.summary: Czechia applies the Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin agreement, so a coffin from a party state travels on the departure country's laissez-passer. DE.summary: Germany signed but never ratified the Strasbourg Agreement; it applies the 1937 Berlin agreement, under which a corpse laissez-passer (Leichenpass) from the departure country is the key document. DO.summary: The Dominican consulate in the country of death processes the shipping documents: for a body, the original death certificate from the vital records office, a certificate of no contagious disease from the local health department, and a notarised embalming certificate signed by the funeral director or embalmer. EC.summary: Ecuador requires a free sanitary entry authorisation (autorizacion sanitaria de ingreso) issued by the Ministry of Public Health office at the international airport or border post of arrival, on presentation of an apostilled, Spanish-translated death certificate, an embalming certificate and the transfer permit from the country of death (Regulation 000001-2022, art. 34). EE.summary: Under the Estonian Cemeteries Act, a deceased person brought into or out of Estonia must travel in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin filled with a desiccant, inside a tightly closed wooden box. EG.summary: To bring the casket of an Egyptian national into Egypt, the Egyptian embassy or consulate in the country of death certifies and translates the death certificate and issues a permit to transport the body to Egypt. at_a_glance.permit: Burial or transit permit from origin

steps.what: Contact the Iraqi embassy or consulate in the country of death and appoint a funeral home.
Obtain the local death certificate and have it authenticated or apostilled.
File the Iraqi death registration online and book the consular appointment.
Submit the written request naming the arrival airport and pay any transport fee.
Fly the sealed casket to the named airport; family or funeral service collects after clearance.

key_points: The consular request must name the entry airport
Fee of USD 3,200 listed for non-Iraqi remains (Washington embassy)
Late penalties if registered after 30 days
Kurdistan Region has its own representation; check which office handles the case

Embassy No Objection letter required by Iraqi authorities

IS.summary: Iceland is a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement, so a coffin from another party state travels on the laissez-passer of the country of death. Under Regulation 618/2018 on the handling and transport of corpses, every body entering Iceland must be in an airtight, watertight container inside a sturdy coffin and carry a packaging certificate and a doctor's certificate on contagious disease.

Obtain death certificate, doctor's contagion certificate and laissez-passer
Body placed in airtight container inside a sturdy coffin; packaging certificate issued
Flight to Iceland with all certificates attached to the coffin
Customs clearance at Keflavik; funeral director arranges burial or cremation

key_points: Strasbourg Agreement party since 11 November 1975
Regulation 618/2018 requires airtight inner container
Missing certificates trigger Chief Epidemiologist procedures
Laissez-passer issuer: District Medical Officer
export_points: Laissez-passer from the District Medical Officer (Strasbourg states)
Airtight inner container in a sturdy coffin
Packaging certificate and doctor's contagion certificate
Post-mortem or police inquiry can delay release

IT.summary: Italy is not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement. From countries outside the 1937 Berlin Agreement, the Italian consulate in the country of death must first obtain the entry authorisation (nulla osta) of the Italian municipality of burial, then issues a mortuary passport; from Berlin Agreement states, the departure authority's mortuary passport is used.

at_a_glance.permit: Municipal nulla osta of burial place

steps.what: Appoint funeral directors; obtain death and medical certificates
Apostille and translate documents; file them with the Italian consulate
Consulate obtains the municipal nulla osta, then issues the mortuary passport
Treatment and sealing in welded zinc and wood coffin when consulate confirms
Funeral director takes coffin by road to the authorised cemetery

key_points: Municipal clearance of the burial place comes first
Allow about 2-3 weeks for consular processing
No onward air transport inside Italy
Consular fees, apostilles and translations are paid by the family
export_points: Mortuary passport (Berlin states) or transport authorisation
Destination consulate clearance for non-Berlin countries
Double zinc and wood coffin; preservation treatment
Allow up to 2 weeks for local formalities
IT.private_jet_note: Fly direct to the airport nearest the burial place; no onward domestic flight is allowed.

The body must be embalmed and in a leak-proof container (hermetically sealed casket if death was from a quarantinable disease), and arrival must be notified at least 24 hours ahead.

JO.summary: A foreign death certificate for a Jordanian must be attested by the Jordanian embassy (or MOFA route) and translated into Arabic by a certified centre; detailed casket import rules are not published, so confirm with the Jordanian consulate. KG.summary: No official Kyrgyz rules for bringing a casket in were found; confirm with the Kyrgyz consulate in the country of death. For bodies leaving Kyrgyzstan, a transfer permit and a zinc coffin sealing report are required, and local formalities take about 7 days.

KH.summary: A body is brought into Cambodia with the support of the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in the country of death; the Canberra embassy asks for the original death certificate, a funeral home letter, a hospital letter that the death was natural, not contagious and the body safe to transport, the flight itinerary and a processing fee. KN.summary: The receiving funeral home in Saint Kitts and Nevis files the departure documents with the Ministry of Health (Chief Medical Officer, via the Basseterre Health Centre), which issues a letter permitting the remains to be shipped in. KR.summary: Korea's Quarantine Act requires anyone bringing a body into the country to submit documents to the chief of the quarantine station at the port of entry: the death certificate (or post-mortem certificate), a copy of the air waybill and, if the death was caused by a quarantinable infectious disease, an embalming certificate. Korean embassies certify (consular confirmation) the foreign documents, and the casket is released at the Incheon cargo terminal after quarantine and customs clearance.

KY.summary: Bringing a body into the Cayman Islands needs an approval letter from the Department of Environmental Health (DEH): send the Importation of Human Remains Request Form with the death certificate (cause of death, communicable or not), burial transit permit and letter of non-communicable disease at least 48 hours before arrival, and present the approval to Customs.
